note: The house museum's own biographies of the family, written from its collection (Frances Glessner's journal, George Glessner's photographs). Later scholarship by the institution that holds the papers, not period evidence; it is cited for facts about the people, never for the 1904 fabric. Two of its facts bear on who lived at 1800 Prairie Avenue in 1904 and are why this record does not put the grown children there: the daughter Frances married in February 1898 and 'within a few years' moved one block north into 1700 S. Prairie Avenue, one of two twin townhouses her parents built for their children; the son George married in June 1898. Where it and the 1923 Story of a House overlap (the 1898 wedding in the parlor), they agree.
